title: Open Visual Translation Memory (VTM) v1.0
description: A translation memory that preserves how text looked, not just what it said: source and target strings anchored to a region of an image, with the typography needed to re-render them faithfully.

vtm_version.description: Format version. Readers implementing 1.x MUST accept any 1.y document and ignore keys they do not recognise.

generator.description: What produced this document. Provenance, not identity -- consumers MUST NOT branch on it.

source_language.description: Document-level source language. Entries MAY override.

target_language.description: Document-level target language. Entries MAY override.

asset.description: The image the geometry belongs to. REQUIRED: a bbox is uninterpretable without the resolution it was recorded against -- (10,20,100,30) describes a different region on a 640px thumbnail than on a 4096px original.

sha256.description: Optional content hash, so a memory can be tied to an exact asset.

bbox.description: Axis-aligned rectangle in PIXELS. Origin is the top-left of the asset; x increases rightward, y increases downward. Named keys rather than a 4-tuple: array ordering is the most common source of silent interop bugs in this shape.

polygon.description: Optional tighter outline in the same pixel space, for rotated or curved text the bbox over-covers.

rotation.description: Baseline rotation in degrees, counter-clockwise positive.

reading_order.description: Position in the asset's reading sequence. Matters for multi-region signage where order carries meaning.

style.description: Portable typography. Deliberately a SUBSET of what a renderer may know: every key here is one a competing implementation can reasonably honour. Engine-specific controls belong under an x- extension.

weight.description: e.g. 'normal', 'bold', or a numeric CSS weight as a string.

background.description: What the text sat on. Enables a consumer to erase and re-render, not merely to read.

provenance.description: How much to trust this entry. A visual TM that reuses a low-confidence pair is worse than one that reuses nothing.

confidence.description: Recognition confidence for the SOURCE text.

qa_score.description: Quality of the rendered TARGET, if it was rendered and scored.

glyph_fallback.description: True when the requested face lacked coverage and a substitute was used.

visual.description: Fingerprints for matching this entry against a region of a DIFFERENT asset -- the mechanism that makes a visual TM reusable rather than merely archival.

phash.description: Perceptual hash of the source region crop.

source.description: Text as it appears in the asset.

^x-.description: Vendor extension. Readers MUST ignore x- keys they do not recognise, and MUST NOT let their absence change interpretation of the standard keys.
